summary: Somalia launched an official eVisa system in 2025 that in principle covers all foreign visitors, but in practice most travelers still receive a 30-day visa on arrival at Mogadishu's Aden Adde airport for about USD 60. The self-declared Republic of Somaliland runs its own, entirely separate entry regime.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Somalia.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Checks are inconsistent, but carry the certificate if you have transited East or Central Africa.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Malaria is present across southern Somalia, including Mogadishu. Antimalarial tablets, repellent and bed nets are strongly recommended — talk to a travel clinic before your trip.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

travelInsurance.text: No insurance is checked on entry, but standard travel policies almost universally exclude Somalia — visitors need specialist cover that includes medical evacuation, which is complex and expensive to arrange from Mogadishu.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

onwardTicket.text: Not formally enforced, but airlines may ask for a return ticket, and most visitors travel with a host organization or fixer who arranges airport clearance and security in advance.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; immigration officers may ask about the purpose of your visit and your host arrangements.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

currencyLimits.text: Somalia publishes no reliable customs thresholds. Declare large amounts of foreign currency on arrival to avoid problems on departure.

source.name: Somalia eVisa — Immigration and Citizenship Agency

notes: Alcohol is illegal in Somalia and may not be brought into the country.
Narcotics are strictly prohibited; khat is legal and widely traded domestically.

payments.text: Somalia runs on US dollar cash and mobile money — services such as EVC Plus dominate daily payments, and shilling notes are used mainly for small change. Card acceptance is rare outside a handful of Mogadishu hotels; bring clean, recent USD notes.

safety.text: Virtually every government advises against all travel to Somalia due to terrorism, armed conflict, crime and a very high kidnapping risk. Al-Shabaab regularly attacks hotels, government sites and the airport road in Mogadishu, and visitors move with pre-arranged armed security. Somaliland (Hargeisa) is calmer but remains covered by do-not-travel advisories.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Somalia Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to February — the Jilal dry season — is the coolest, driest window; the Gu rains fall roughly April to June, and the coast is hot and humid for much of the year.

tips.text: Somalia is under do-not-travel advisories from virtually every government — terrorism and kidnapping risks are severe, independent tourism is effectively impossible, and visitors travel with armed escorts arranged before arrival.

Somaliland runs its own entry regime — flights to Hargeisa require a separate Somaliland visa (issued on arrival or through its missions for many nationalities), and federal Somali visas are not accepted there, nor Somaliland visas in Mogadishu.

The 2025 eVisa is officially mandatory, but airline and airport practice has been inconsistent during the transition. Apply online if you can, and carry USD 60–65 in cash as a fallback for the visa on arrival.
Bring clean, recent US dollar notes — cash dollars and mobile money pay for nearly everything, and ATMs accepting foreign cards are scarce and unreliable.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Somalia?
faq.answer: Yes — every foreign visitor needs a visa. Somalia launched an official eVisa in 2025, and in practice most travelers can still obtain a 30-day visa on arrival at Mogadishu's Aden Adde airport for about USD 60, paid in cash. Confirm current practice with your airline before flying.

faq.question: Is it safe to travel to Somalia?
faq.answer: No — Somalia is one of the highest-risk destinations in the world. Governments advise against all travel due to terrorism, kidnapping and armed conflict, and the few visitors who go travel with professional security arranged in advance.

faq.question: Is Somaliland's visa different from Somalia's?
faq.answer: Yes. The self-declared Republic of Somaliland controls its own borders: travelers flying into Hargeisa need a Somaliland visa, and a Somali federal visa or eVisa is not valid there. The two entry systems are completely separate.

faq.question: Can I pay for the Somali visa on arrival in cash?
faq.answer: Yes. The visa on arrival at Mogadishu is paid in US dollars cash (about USD 60). Bring clean, undamaged notes, as worn or older bills are often refused.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Somalia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, which includes much of East and Central Africa. Checks are inconsistent, but carry your ICVP certificate if your route passes through a risk country.
